title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 36
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 36: Sennacherib attacks Judah and Rabshakeh mocks Hezekiah's trust in Yahweh before the wall of Jerusalem.

questions.text: In the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, who attacked the fortified cities of Judah?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 36:1 says that Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

questions.text: From which city did the king of Assyria send Rabshakeh to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to king Hezekiah with a large army.

questions.text: To what did Rabshakeh compare Egypt, in which Judah trusted?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh called Egypt the staff of a bruised reed, which pierces the hand of the man who leans on it.

answers.text: The staff of a bruised reed
A flower fading in the field

questions.text: What did Rabshakeh offer to give if Judah could set riders on them?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh said he would give two thousand horses, if they were able on their part to set riders on them.

questions.text: In which language did Eliakim, Shebna and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak?
questions.explanation: They asked him to speak in Aramaic, which they understood, and not in the Jews' language in the hearing of the people on the wall.

questions.text: What did Rabshakeh do after being asked not to speak in the Jews' language?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh stood and called out with a loud voice in the Jews' language, telling the people to hear the words of the king of Assyria.

answers.text: He began to speak to them in Aramaic
He went back to his master without a word
He called out loudly in the Jews' language
He wrote his message down in a letter instead

questions.text: What did the king of Assyria promise each person who made peace and came out to him?
questions.explanation: He promised that each one would eat from his vine and his fig tree and drink the waters of his own cistern.

answers.text: To receive a house and a field in the land of Assyria
To serve as officers in the king's own palace
To receive a share of the spoil taken from Egypt
To eat from his own vine and fig tree and drink from his own cistern

questions.text: The gods of which places did Rabshakeh say had failed to deliver their lands?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh asked where the gods of Hamath and Arpad were, and where the gods of Sepharvaim were.

questions.text: Why did the people on the wall say nothing in reply to Rabshakeh?
questions.explanation: They remained silent because the king's commandment was, "Don't answer him."

answers.text: They could not understand his words
They were too afraid to speak
The king had commanded them not to answer him
They had already agreed to surrender

questions.text: In what state did Eliakim, Shebna and Joah come to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: They came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
